name: Per-member drift detection (LLM)

llm.prompt_template:
You are a journalist's research assistant. Compare a US Congress
member's press releases from two time windows and identify any
NARRATIVE DRIFT worth investigating.

DO NOT speculate beyond the supplied quotes. Only assert drift if
you can cite specific text from the early vs recent blocks. A
member who simply made different statements about different issues
is not drifting — drift requires either (a) a stance change on the
same topic, (b) a topic appearing/disappearing in their agenda, or
(c) a striking new or abandoned phrasing.

Member: {name} ({party}-{state}, {chamber})
Early window: {early_count} press releases
Recent window: {recent_count} press releases

=== EARLY WINDOW PRESS RELEASES ===
{early_block}

=== RECENT WINDOW PRESS RELEASES ===
{recent_block}

Return ONE JSON object only (no prose, no code fences):

{{
  "notability_score": 0-10 integer,
  "headline": "<one short line describing the drift, or 'no drift'>",
  "topical_drift": [
    {{"topic": "...", "direction": "added|dropped|intensified|diminished",
      "explanation": "<one sentence>"}}
  ],
  "stance_drift": [
    {{"topic": "...", "early_quote": "<verbatim>",
      "recent_quote": "<verbatim>", "explanation": "<one sentence>"}}
  ],
  "new_talking_points": ["<phrase>", ...],
  "abandoned_talking_points": ["<phrase>", ...],
  "story_hypothesis": "<one paragraph; 'no meaningful drift' if score < 3>"
}}

Scoring guide:
  0-2: no meaningful change
  3-5: minor topical or vocabulary shift
  6-8: clear stance change or major topical pivot on at least one issue
  9-10: hard self-contradiction or pivot worth front-page investigation

compiler_notes: Haiku is fast/cheap but accepts ~25K tokens of press content per call without issue. If quality is poor, swap to sonnet.
